extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in real analysis/measure theory (and instructors reading the chapter)
extracted.subtask_description: Textbook exposition of Lp spaces: basic properties, inequalities (Hölder, Minkowski), completeness, convolution properties, measure decompositions (Jordan/Hahn/Radon–Nikodym), and the identification of the continuous dual of Lp (Riesz representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator functions of finite-measure sets lie in Lp and generate Lp
rubrics_metrics.description: Every indicator function of a set of finite measure is in Lp(X), and the smallest closed subspace of Lp(X) containing all such indicator functions is Lp(X) itself (for 1 ≤ p < ∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is used to reduce many density and approximation questions to simple functions supported on sets of finite measure; it is proved similarly to Proposition 5.56 and underlies the density results that follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple functions from finite-measure sets lie in every Lp and are dense
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of simple functions built from sets of finite measure lies in every Lp(X) for 1 ≤ p < ∞, and their linear span (and closure) is Lp(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct consequence of the previous item and standard approximation arguments (Proposition 5.55d, monotone convergence where needed). Useful when approximating general Lp functions by simple functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusions among Lp spaces (relations for different p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations between Lp spaces for different indices p1 ≤ p ≤ p2 are established: intersections of L^{p1} and L^{p2} sit in intermediate Lp spaces, and decompositions f = f1 + f2 (with f1 in L^{p1}, f2 in L^{p2}) are used to prove inclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proofs proceed by splitting a function into parts where |f| ≤ 1 and |f| > 1 and applying integrability estimates; special handling when p2 = ∞. Use the splitting technique shown in the proof (f = f1 + f2 with f1 handling |f| ≤ 1 and f2 the tail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hölder-based interpolation inequality (Proposition 9.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 1 ≤ p1 < p < p2 ≤ ∞ and t ∈ [0,1] chosen so 1/p = (1−t)/p1 + t/p2, then for f in L^{p1} ∩ L^{p2} one has ||f||_p ≤ ||f||_{p1}^{1−t} ||f||_{p2}^t (with the usual modifications when p2 = ∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by choosing appropriate auxiliary exponents and applying Hölder's inequality (and essential supremum when p2 = ∞). This gives a quantitative interpolation bound between Lp norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of Lp (Theorem 9.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ (with usual caveats), Lp(X,µ) is complete: every Cauchy sequence in Lp has a subsequence converging pointwise almost everywhere to an a.e. limit f, and the original sequence converges to f in Lp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces to the p = 1 case (Theorem 5.58) and uses the standard subsequence-and-dominated-convergence arguments. The detailed formulation ensures compatibility of limits across different p-spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minkowski's inequality for integrals (Theorem 9.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f(x,y) is measurable on the product of σ-finite measure spaces X×Y, then (∫_X (∫_Y |f(x,y)| dν(y))^p dµ(x))^{1/p} ≤ ∫_Y (∫_X |f(x,y)|^p dµ(x))^{1/p} dν(y) (with measurability and finiteness caveats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Fubini's theorem and Hölder's inequality; special care is taken about measurability and handling the division by factors that may be infinite by approximation with bounded functions supported on finite-measure rectangles and monotone convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lp norm equality via dual sup (Proposition 9.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞ with dual index p0, ||f||_p = sup{ ∫ f g dµ : g ∈ L^{p0}, ||g||_{p0} ≤ 1 } when µ is σ-finite (and a suitable statement for p = ∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction uses Hölder; the reverse constructs a maximizing g from f (or uses approximations) to show equality. Note: equality can fail if µ is not σ-finite (example referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of C_c(V) and separability for Borel measures (Proposition 9.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ is a Borel measure on a nonempty open subset V of R^N and 1 ≤ p < ∞, then (a) C_c(V) is dense in Lp(V,µ), (b) the closed subspace generated by indicator functions of compact subsets equals Lp(V,µ), and (c) Lp(V,µ) is separable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses regularity of Borel measures, previous density results for simple functions, and standard corollaries (Lemma 6.22c, Theorem 6.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convolution inequalities involving Lp (Proposition 9.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional convolution mapping results: e.g., if f ∈ L^1 and g ∈ L^p (or vice versa) then f * g ∈ L^p with ||f*g||_p ≤ ||f||_1 ||g||_p; if f ∈ L^p and g ∈ L^{p0} then f*g is bounded and ||f*g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_p ||g||_{p0}; other standard Young-type inequalities are enumerated for 1 < p < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs follow from Minkowski's integral inequality and Hölder's inequality just as the p=2 special cases were handled earlier (cf. Proposition 6.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of translation in Lp (Proposition 9.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 1 ≤ p < ∞ and f ∈ L^p(R^N), then the translation operator τ_t f(x) = f(x−t) is continuous in the translation parameter: lim_{t→0} ||τ_t f − f||_p = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from density of C_c (compactly supported continuous functions) in Lp and the fact that translations are continuous on those dense subspaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convolution of Lp and L^{p0} gives bounded uniformly continuous function (Proposition 9.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 1 ≤ p < ∞ and p0 is the dual index, then convolution of f ∈ L^p with g ∈ L^{p0} yields a bounded, uniformly continuous function and ||f*g||_∞ ≤ ||f||_p ||g||_{p0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends the L^2/L^2 case; proof uses previous convolution inequalities and translation continuity to show uniform continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation by mollifiers (Theorem 9.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let φ ∈ L^1(R^N), set φ_ε(x) = ε^{-N} φ(x/ε) and let c = ∫ φ. For f ∈ L^p with 1 ≤ p < ∞, lim_{ε→0} || f * φ_ε − c f ||_p = 0 (with usual normalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from Minkowski's inequality for integrals and continuity of translation in Lp; standard tool for approximation and smoothing in Lp spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jordan decomposition for bounded additive set functions (Proposition 9.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bounded additive real-valued set function ν on an algebra A has nonnegative bounded additive components ν^+ and ν^− such that ν = ν^+ − ν^−; ν^+ and ν^− are minimal among decompositions into nonnegative bounded additive set functions; if ν is completely additive, so are ν^+ and ν^−.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct ν^+ as supremum of ν(F) over F ⊆ E and ν^− similarly; verify additivity and minimality. This prepares for Jordan/Hahn decompositions for signed measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hahn decomposition for bounded signed measures (Theorem 9.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ν is a bounded signed measure on a σ-algebra A, there exist disjoint measurable sets P and N partitioning X such that ν(E) ≥ 0 for all measurable E ⊆ P and ν(E) ≤ 0 for all measurable E ⊆ N (i.e., a Hahn decomposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs approximating sets with controlled ν^+ and ν^− and uses complete additivity; nonuniqueness occurs on µ-null sets. This decomposition underlies the Radon–Nikodym argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radon–Nikodym Theorem (Theorem 9.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let µ and ν be σ-finite measures on (X,A) and ν ≪ µ. Then there exists a measurable f ≥ 0 with ν(E) = ∫_E f dµ for all measurable E, and f is unique up to µ-a.e. equality. (Extension to complex-valued completely additive ν also treated.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces first to the finite-measure case, uses supremum constructions and Hahn decompositions, and then patches local finite-measure results via σ-finiteness. Uniqueness shown by considering difference of two candidates and using σ-finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lebesgue decomposition (Corollary 9.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given σ-finite µ and a σ-finite measure ν, ν decomposes uniquely as ν = f dµ + ν_s where ν_s is singular with respect to µ (concentrated on a µ-null set) and f ∈ L^1(µ) is the Radon–Nikodym derivative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction via taking supremum of ν on sets of arbitrarily small µ-measure and applying Radon–Nikodym to the absolutely continuous part; uniqueness follows from uniqueness in Radon–Nikodym and support properties of singular measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz representation theorem for Lp dual (Theorem 9.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X,A,µ) is σ-finite and 1 ≤ p < ∞ with dual index p0, then every continuous linear functional x* on L^p(X,µ) has the form x*(f) = ∫ f g dµ for a unique g ∈ L^{p0}(X,µ); moreover ||x*|| = ||g||_{p0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the finite-additive set function E ↦ x*(1_E), show it is a (countably additive) measure absolutely continuous w.r.t. µ, apply Radon–Nikodym to obtain g, and extend linearity and integrability arguments to all L^p. Handle complex scalars by separating real and imaginary parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks on duality exceptions and separability
rubrics_metrics.description: If µ is not σ-finite, the representation of the dual of L^p by L^{p0} can fail (examples exist for L^∞ and for counting measure on ℕ). Separability of L^p (e.g., for Borel measures on open sets) allows weak-* compactness arguments via Alaoglu when identifying duals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of pathologies when σ-finiteness fails (construct non-completely-additive bounded additive set functions leading to linear functionals not represented by L^1 functions). Use separability results (Proposition 9.9) for functional-analytic applications like extracting weak-* convergent subsequences in duals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz–Thorin convexity context (intro to Section 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preview: linear operators between Lp spaces satisfy interpolation-type norm inequalities; the Riesz–Thorin Convexity Theorem (complex-analytic method) gives sharp operator-norm estimates for a one-parameter family of spaces when endpoints are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section will define operator types (p→q) and outline that boundedness on endpoints plus complex interpolation yields bounds for intermediate p; simple functions are dense and are used to verify the estimates on dense subspaces before extension by continuity.
